subject.title: fix(providers): bind cleanup to live cloud ownership

question: After the AWS provider-key fallback bug is fixed, should direct AWS, Azure, and GCP cleanup fail closed when exact local claims or live provider ownership proof are missing?
rationale: The patch changes the destructive cleanup boundary and can retain claims or cloud residue for workflows that older cleanup deleted, so final landing needs maintainer acceptance even after the mechanical blocker is repaired.

options.title: Fix And Land
options.body: Repair the AWS explicit-provider-key gap, remove release-owned changelog edits, and merge with maintainer-owned acceptance of the stricter cleanup boundary.

options.title: Split By Provider
options.body: Land AWS, Azure, and GCP hardening as separate PRs if maintainers want smaller compatibility review units.

options.title: Pause For Recovery Policy
options.body: Hold the branch until maintainers define a separate recovery or strict-mode policy for legacy cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Fix And Land
recommendation.body: Repair the AWS explicit-provider-key gap, remove release-owned changelog edits, and merge with maintainer-owned acceptance of the stricter cleanup boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The direct cleanup baseline and this PR's provider hardening both route through recent provider cleanup history tied to steipete.
